name: Royal Manas National Park
blurb: Tall grass, tigers, rhinos and rare langurs on the Manas floodplain.

tip.title: Lose the tall grass
tip.text: Tall wet grassland shelters pygmy hogs, hog deer and floricans. Cut Tall grasses and watch them, then the tiger and leopard, respond.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm subtropical sun fuels fast growth of grasses and forest trees through the long wet season.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Heavy rain falls between May and September, about 333 cm a year in the Manas area, and drives growth and flooding.

nodes.name: Manas River floods
nodes.desc: The Manas River and its tributaries spread silt across the plains and keep the early-growth riverside grassland renewed.

nodes.name: Grassland fire
nodes.desc: Periodic burning has kept tall grassland open, though Wikipedia notes it can also threaten pygmy hogs sheltering in it.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead grass, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Tall grasses
nodes.desc: Tall wet grassland of cogon and Saccharum grasses that can reach several metres. It gives food, cover and nesting material to many grassland animals.

nodes.name: Forest canopy trees
nodes.desc: Semi-evergreen and deciduous forest trees such as lampati make up the forest cover of the northern park, feeding leaf and fruit eaters.

nodes.name: Siam weed
nodes.desc: A fast-spreading invasive shrub of disturbed ground. GloBI has records of elephants eating it.

nodes.name: Hog deer
nodes.desc: A small deer of tall, moist grassland. It is a recorded tiger and leopard prey species here.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A large deer of the forest and its edges, recorded in the park and eaten by tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: Wild water buffalo
nodes.desc: Large grazing bovine of the grassland, which is listed among the herbivores of the Manas area.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: Eats grass, browse and the invasive Siam weed. Its feeding and trampling shape open ground in forest and grassland.

nodes.name: Indian rhinoceros
nodes.desc: A grassland grazer; Royal Manas is the only Bhutanese park where it lives.

nodes.name: Pygmy hog
nodes.desc: An omnivore of tall dense grassland that digs roots and tubers and shelters in grass-lined nests. The only known wild population is at Manas.

nodes.name: Golden langur
nodes.desc: A tree-dwelling leaf, fruit, seed and flower eater found only in a small area of Bhutan and Assam.

nodes.name: Bengal florican
nodes.desc: Endangered bird of tall grassland; Manas holds the largest population anywhere according to Wikipedia.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: Rooting omnivore recorded in the park and listed as tiger and leopard prey in GloBI.

nodes.name: Indian hare
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating hare recorded near the park; GloBI lists it as prey of tigers, leopards and civets.

nodes.name: Burmese python
nodes.desc: A large constrictor. Wikipedia says pythons are among the predators of pygmy hogs.

nodes.name: Bengal monitor
nodes.desc: A large ground lizard that eats insects, small mammals including hares, and scavenges carcasses such as deer.

nodes.name: Asian palm civet
nodes.desc: Omnivore of forest and edges; GloBI records it eating Indian hares.

nodes.name: Tiger
nodes.desc: Top predator, recorded taking hog deer, sambar, wild boar, buffalo and hares in GloBI, and pygmy hogs per Wikipedia.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Apex predator of forest and grassland edge. GloBI records it eating deer, boar, hares, civets and golden langurs.
